status.en: 8 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 60% more than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Oromo.
status.nb: 8 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 60 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Oromo.

summary.en: Ethiopia is deepening its regional involvement by offering to host Sudanese dialogue and urging Sudanese parties to join mediation, while Ethiopian-linked drones killed four people and damaged a United Nations building in Khartoum. Ethiopian forces shelled Alamata, killing 14 civilians and prompting Amnesty International to call for a war crimes investigation in Tigray. Intelligence suggests coordination between Eritrean and Sudanese actors in drone strikes on Mekelle and Assosa. Ethiopian troops have regained control of border areas near Badme and clashes continue along the Afar-Somali border over territory, drought and resources. 2,824 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopia utdyper sitt regionale engasjement ved å tilby å være vert for sudansk dialog og oppfordre sudanske parter til å delta i mekling, mens droner med etiopisk tilknytning drepte fire personer og skadet en FN-bygning i Khartoum. Etiopiske styrker skjøt mot Alamata, drepte 14 sivile og fikk Amnesty International til å kreve en etterforskning av krigsforbrytelser i Tigray. Etterretning tyder på koordinering mellom eritreiske og sudanske aktører i droneangrep på Mekelle og Assosa. Etiopiske tropper har gjenvunnet kontroll over grenseområder ved Badme, og kamper fortsetter langs grensen mellom Afar og Somali om territorium, tørke og ressurser. 2 824 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.

The incident marked the first reported attack on a UN compound in Khartoum since the Sudanese army recaptured the capital in May 2025. The UN statement attributed the attacks to the Rapid Support Forces (#RSF), saying they were “reportedly launched by the RSF.” The paramilitary group has been fighting Sudan’s national army since April 2023.
